problem: Evaluating MLLMs as embodied navigation agents is costly (simulator rendering) and fragmented; prior suites like NavBench fix a single agent design, so model limits cannot be separated from prompting/agent engineering, and results are mostly aggregate metrics without error diagnosis.
motivation: VLN needs 3D spatial reasoning, long-term memory and multi-round contextual reasoning, so it is a demanding test of MLLMs as agents. A cheap, modular, simulator-free harness allows systematic Model x Agent x Task comparison and fine-grained failure analysis, which can guide MLLM post-training for embodied use.
key_idea: A modular, simulator-free VLN evaluation framework (pre-rendered 4-view observations on discrete nav graphs, swappable Model/Agent/Task) used to diagnose zero-shot MLLM agents, revealing looping failures and a perception-action gap.
insight: Adding CoT and/or self-reflection to NavGPT/MapGPT-style agents often lowers performance (e.g. Qwen2.5-VL-7B fine-grained SR 27.5 -> 21.0 with CoT), and map memory gives little gain, because MLLMs reason locally and ignore history rather than lacking perception. Error analysis (106 of 131 navigation errors are looping) and diagnostic study (oracle reasoning assistant lifts SR 0 -> 52 on hard negatives; failure-example ICL lifts SR to 12-16) indicate the bottleneck is strategic planning/history utilization, not visual recognition.
method: Model/Task/Agent abstractions: factory-pattern plug-and-play modules coordinated by a Runner with lightweight configs, logging for post-hoc analysis

Curated benchmark: stratified subsets of val-unseen from R2R (fine-grained), REVERIE (coarse-grained), and MP3D ObjectNav (zero-grained), balanced over scene, path length, instruction and object category; 200/300/200-style subsets validated against full splits (SR/SPL within ~2-3 points)

Simulator-free environment: pre-rendered four 90° FoV perspective images per viewpoint reoriented to agent heading (Left/Front/Right/Back), numbered markers for navigable candidates; VRAM ~1.7GB vs ~10GB and 8.8x faster observation access than Habitat
Semantic metadata: GPT-5 marker captions and BLIP-2 + GPT-5 viewpoint summaries for text-memory agents

Eight agent variants: NavGPT-style text-summarization history and MapGPT-style text topological map, each with baseline, CoT, Reflection, CoT+Reflection; rule-based action parsing with re-prompting on invalid output
Diagnostics: Gradio trajectory visualizer, manual failure/success categorization, hard-negative case study with Qwen3VL-4B oracle assistant and failure-aware few-shot ICL

setting.backbone: GPT-5, Gemini-2.5 Pro, Qwen2.5-VL-7B, InternVL3-2B/8B, LLaVA-OneVision-7B (all frozen, zero-shot)
setting.observation: four 90° perspective RGB images per viewpoint (agent-centric panorama) with numbered candidate markers plus text captions/history
setting.action_space: discrete nav-graph viewpoint selection (marker ID) plus STOP
setting.simulator: simulator-free (pre-rendered Matterport3D views; R2R, REVERIE, Habitat MP3D ObjectNav episodes)
setting.privileged: none (Oracle assistant Qwen3VL-4B only in the diagnostic case study)

numbers_note: Table 1 contains 8 agent variants x 6 MLLMs x 3 tasks; only NavGPT baseline rows for the top models and Qwen are listed here. MapGPT rows and CoT/Reflection variants exist (e.g. MapGPT Gemini-2.5 Pro fine-grained SR 39.5, SPL 30.72; NavGPT w/ CoT Qwen2.5-VL-7B fine-grained SR 21.00) but not listed. Subset sizes are inferred from SR granularity, not stated explicitly.
results: Proprietary models set the zero-shot upper bound (best fine-grained: Gemini-2.5 Pro NavGPT SR 41.0, SPL 32.67) while Qwen2.5-VL-7B is the strongest open model (SR 27.5). CoT/reflection typically reduce SR, and zero-shot agents remain far below specialists (DUET 72 SR on R2R val-unseen). Object-oriented navigation is the easiest and coarse-grained the hardest.
limitations: Covers only a selection of MLLMs and agent designs, and only R2R/REVERIE/ObjectNav with static English instructions on a discrete graph (no continuous control, dialog, or multilingual tasks)
Diagnostic only: proposes no algorithmic remedy; benchmark is a curated subset with pre-rendered 4-view observations, and the error analysis is on ~200 trajectories from a single model
Reasoning-strategy conclusions rest on prompt-based agents; the hard-negative study is tiny (25 trajectories)
